imem_words.doc: Program memory depth in 32-bit words. Capped in practice at 256 by the ISA: BR and CALL targets are eight bits, so a larger store holds words nothing can jump to. On CMOS5L this is an IHP SRAM macro, 256 words costing 6.9% of a 6x4 die, measured from the PDK LEF; in flip-flops the same depth would exceed the whole die, which is why the storage primitive rather than the depth was ever the constraint. The assembler refuses a program longer than this value. The store is a single-port synchronous-read block in axpe_imem.sv, shaped for that macro; the host can address the first 256 words, since the ISA's branch target cannot reach past them either.

reg_count.doc: General registers R0..R(n-1). Costs reg_count * reg_width flip-flops against a whole-die ceiling near 7,680, so this is one of the few knobs that trades directly against the instruction store.

reg_width.doc: Register width in bits. Also the widest value SHOUT/SHIN can move in one instruction and the widest measurement WAITE can return, so narrowing it shortens the longest interval the chip can time.

delay_bits.doc: Width of the delay field every instruction carries, and therefore the longest single hold or WAITE timeout in cycles. At 50 MHz, 16 bits reaches 1.31 ms, which covers one bit time down to about 763 baud.

uio_pins.doc: Bidirectional protocol pins, each with its own direction and open-drain control. The Tiny Tapeout harness supplies 8; a profile targeting another carrier may have fewer.

call_depth.doc: Hardware call stack entries. Each costs clog2(imem_words) flip-flops. Firmware that exceeds it is a build-time error in the assembler rather than a silent overwrite.
